title: Wednesday Quick Tip
subtitle: Smaller games, more touches
hook: How many times did each kid touch the ball in your last scrimmage?
intro: Three of them never touch it.
statement: Smaller games give every player more turns.
q1: Do you play three on three in small spaces —
q2: or full scrimmages that look like real games?
q3: Who gets more touches in smaller games?
t1: Every team is different. But skills grow faster
t2: when every kid is part of the play.
cta: Coaches — small games or full scrimmage?
ctaLines: Three on three. Four goals. Short games.
ctaPrompt: Share your scrimmage habit below. There are no wrong answers.
caption:
How many times did each kid touch the ball in your last scrimmage?
Ten kids chase one ball. Three of them never touch it.
Smaller games give every player more turns.
Small-sided games or full scrimmages. There is no single right way.
Small games or full scrimmage? Share your habit in the comments.
